title: Delta Industries — initial technical capture
content:
Context:
- Customer: Delta Industries (legacy manufacturing + digital twin initiative). Small AI team, large ops team. Security/compliance: must keep PII out of hosted logs; prefer private deployment in us-west-2 or on-prem air-gapped option for phase 2.
- Meeting: 2025-06-11 11:00 PT — initial scoping with CTO (Anika Rao), Head of AI (Tom B.), Infra lead (Marco).

High-level ask:
- Low-latency, bursty inference for operator chat assistant + batch embedding for search/ranking. Expectation: 50 qps steady for chat (95p latency < 300ms token when possible), spikes to 250 qps during shift change. Embeddings: nightly batch for ~4M docs, incremental daily 50k.
- Data residency: all logs and request payloads for EU customers must not leave EU region; initial pilot is US only.
- Security: KMS integration mandatory, SOC2/audit logs required.

Technical details noted on call (informal capture):
- Primary model family: open-llama-like architecture (they prefer open models). They want to test both 7B and 13B variants.
- Typical prompt lengths: user messages ~30-60 tokens, context + system + recent turns ~1.5k tokens on average; long troubleshooting sessions can go to 8k.
- Throughput profile: many short synchronous chat requests from embedded operator console; also async bulk API for embeddings.
- Latency SLO: operator UX expects <350ms median token latency for realtime; they said they can tolerate higher when model >13B. Need to translate to server SLOs (per-token or per-response?).
- Budget: initial pilot budget flagged as $5k/month for hosted and limited POC; likely bump to reserved capacity if results promising.

Immediate gotchas / risks called out:
- Their infra uses a homegrown proxy that strips/rewrites headers; we may need to support custom header pass-through or a sidecar. Action: get sample proxy config. // Action A1
- Their model ops team concerned about KV cache correctness across restarts; they have long conversations and rely on consistent streaming tokens for UI. Need to confirm that prefix/KV caching and warmup behavior will not cause duplicate tokens after failover. // Action A2
- EU data residency requirement will block any hosted logging to our global analytics pipeline without a per-customer regional isolation plan. This is typical but flagged early.

Proposed pilot architecture (notes from us):
- Private deployment (VPC) in their AWS account in us-west-2 using Redwood Private control plane with KMS integration. Start with a small Dedicated-like pool (2x A10G equiv) for 7B, and optional 13B on burst nodes.
- Use continuous prefix caching for repeated operator prompts; configure short TTL for troubleshooting logs (30d) to satisfy their retention policy.
- Embedding pipeline: run batch embed job on dedicated spot fleet overnight; store vectors in their existing FAISS/Elastic cluster.

Questions to resolve (open):
- Q1: exact QPS distribution shape (we have median vs peak, need 95/99-percentile concurrency). // Ask: can they share a 2-week scrape?
- Q2: expected concurrent long-context sessions (8k tokens) — how many at peak? This affects memory footprint and kernel selection.
- Q3: do they need live transcript retention for >90 days? Compliance will push us toward encrypted long-term storage.

Action items (owner initials + rough ETA):
- A1: Get sample proxy config + example request (Maya) — ETA 2025-06-16.
- A2: Confirm KV cache semantics on model restarts + get infra test case from runtime team (Ethan) — ETA 2025-06-20.
- A3: Draft pilot cost estimate comparing hosted vs private (2 node vs 4 node cluster) and include cost per 1M tokens (Maya + Lina) — ETA 2025-06-18.
- A4: Provision sandbox in their AWS account (minimal infra skeleton + KMS demo) (Infra eng: Marco) — blocking until we get IAM playbook from their infra.
- A5: Create evaluation prompt set for operator flows (3 categories: triage, repair, escalate) (Tom B. to share examples) — ETA 2025-06-21.

Notes to self (rough thoughts):
- Consider recommending quantized 13B runtime to reduce memory and lower latency for 8k contexts; need to check quality deltas on their prompts.
- Add a fallback policy: 7B for standard operations; route to 13B only for flagged long-context or hard-reasoning queries to save cost.
- Could offer a led model warmup window before shift changes (schedule pre-warm scaling) to handle the 250 qps spike.

Follow ups scheduled / calendar:
- 2025-06-18: tech deep-dive with runtime eng (Ethan + Maya + Marco + Tom) — agenda: KV cache, streaming behavior, proxy tests.
- 2025-06-25: cost and SLAs review with procurement + product.

Relevant links / artifacts (quick refs):
- Infra ticket: INF-3789 (integration skeleton + kube templates).
- Confluence draft: delta-integration-playbook-824 (contains early compliance checklist).
- Sandbox repo: github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning/tree/feature/delta-templates

Loose transcript highlights (verbatim-ish):
- Anika (CTO): "We can't have operator sessions interrupted; if warmup means we lose tokens, that's no-go." (underline that A2 is important).
- Tom (Head of AI): "Budget small for now but if latency + cost look good, we'll move to reserved capacity in Q3."

Closing: keep this doc as scratch — we'll formalize into a one-pager for procurement once we have cost numbers. Main near-term blockers: proxy example + KV cache test case.

End of notes.
